'''Thomas Craig Brown''' (born 1938) is an American-Canadian [[mathematician]], Ramsey Theorist, and [[Professor Emeritus]] at [[Simon Fraser University]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Tom Brown Professor Emeritus at SFU |url=https://www.sfu.ca/math/department/faculty/brown--tom.html |accessdate=10 November 2020}}</ref>

== Collaborations ==
As a mathematician, Brown’s primary focus in his research is in the field of [[Ramsey theory|Ramsey Theory]]. When completing his Ph.D., his thesis was 'On Semigroups which are Unions of Periodic Groups'<ref>{{cite book |last1=Jensen |first1=Gary R. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=BZIbCAAAQBAJ |title=150 Years of Mathematics at Washington University in St. Louis |last2=Krantz |first2=Steven G. |date=2006 |publisher=American Mathematical Society |isbn=978-0-8218-3603-3 |page=15}}</ref> In 1963 as a graduate student, he showed that if the positive integers are finitely colored, then some color class is ''piece-wise syndetic''.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Brown |first1=T. C. |title=An interesting combinatorial method in the theory of locally finite semigroups. |journal=Pacific Journal of Mathematics |date=1971 |volume=36 |issue=2 |pages=285–289 |doi=10.2140/pjm.1971.36.285 |url=http://people.math.sfu.ca/~vjungic/tbrown/tom-59.pdf|doi-access=free }}</ref>

In ''A Density Version of a Geometric Ramsey Theorem,''<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Brown |first1=T. C. |last2=Buhler |first2=J. P. |title=A Density version of a Geometric Ramsey Theorem |journal=[[Journal of Combinatorial Theory]] | series=Series A |date=1982 |volume=32 |pages=20–34 |doi=10.1016/0097-3165(82)90062-0 |url=http://people.math.sfu.ca/~vjungic/tbrown/tom-51.pdf|doi-access=free }}</ref>  he and [[Joe P. Buhler]] showed that “for every <math>\varepsilon > 0</math> there is an <math>n(\varepsilon)</math> such that if <math>n = dim(V) \geq n(\varepsilon)</math> then any subset of <math>V</math> with more than <math>\varepsilon|V|</math> elements must contain 3 collinear points” where <math>V</math> is an <math>n</math>-dimensional [[affine space]] over the field with <math>p^d</math> elements, and <math>p \neq 2</math>".

In ''Descriptions of the characteristic sequence of an irrational'',<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Brown |first1=T. C. |title=Descriptions of the Characteristic Sequence of an Irrational. |journal=[[Canadian Mathematical Bulletin]] |date=1993 |volume=36 |pages=15–21 |doi=10.4153/CMB-1993-003-6 | doi-access=free |url=http://people.math.sfu.ca/~vjungic/tbrown/tom-31.pdf}}</ref> Brown discusses the following idea: Let <math>\alpha</math> be a positive irrational real number. The characteristic sequence of <math>\alpha</math> is <math>f(\alpha) = f_1 f_2 \ldots </math>; where <math>f_n = [ ( n+1 )\alpha] [\alpha] </math>.” From here he discusses “the various descriptions of the characteristic sequence of α which have appeared in the literature” and refines this description to “obtain a very simple derivation of an arithmetic expression for <math>[n\alpha]</math>.” He then gives some conclusions regarding the conditions for <math>[n\alpha]</math> which are equivalent to <math>f_n = 1</math>.

He has collaborated with [[Paul Erdős]], including ''Quasi-Progressions and Descending Waves''<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Brown |first1=T. C. |last2=Erdős |first2=P. |last3=Freedman |first3=A. R. |title=Quasi-Progressions and Descending Waves |journal=[[Journal of Combinatorial Theory]] | series=Series A |date=1990 |volume=53 |pages=81–95 |doi=10.1016/0097-3165(90)90021-N|doi-access= }}</ref> and ''Quantitative Forms of a Theorem of Hilbert''.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Brown |first1=T. C. |last2=Chung |first2=F. R. K. |last3=Erdős |first3=P. |title=Quantitative Forms of a Theorem of Hilbert |journal=[[Journal of Combinatorial Theory]] | series=Series A |date=1985 |volume=38 |issue=2 |pages=210–216 |doi=10.1016/0097-3165(85)90071-8 |url=http://people.math.sfu.ca/~vjungic/tbrown/tom-42.pdf|doi-access=free }}</ref>
